column11: ANCHOR, Vabysmo, the last new anti-VEGF agent to take share by switching patients already on injections. Its Medicare Part B beneficiaries were 172,503 in 2024 (drug_demand) and 213,777 in 2025 (Part B quarterly file bf6a5b3b-31ee-4abb-b1ad-2607a1e7510a). Net of the 34.7% who stop a year (Kuo BL et al., Ophthalmology Retina 2024;8:1074-1082, as mrk_mk_8748.csv carries it), 2025 new starts are 213,777 - 172,503 x 0.653 = 101,133. The pool they came from is the 2025 Part B beneficiaries on another anti-VEGF agent in the same file: Eylea 222,280, Avastin 97,130, Eylea HD 99,161, Pavblu 80,140, Lucentis 21,507, Cimerli 19,257, Byooviz 2,334, Beovu 1,113 and Susvimo 493, 543,415 in all. Capture 18.61%, level with the 18.3% mrk_mk_8748.csv measured for 2024. MULTIPLE 1/6, A JUDGEMENT: 1/6 x 18.61% = 3.10%, half again the 2% sura-vec carries on this pool. For more: it is given in the office by the same intravitreal injection it replaces, where sura-vec needs vitrectomy and subretinal surgery; OPTIC cut annualised injections by a cumulative 87% through five years (ASRS 2026). Against: the Phase 3 dose is under a third of OPTIC's, with 52 weeks of LUNA data behind it; the five-year OPTIC cohort was 15 patients with mean BCVA down 6.1 letters (90% CI -15.9 to 3.7); both trials are designed against aflibercept 2 mg every 8 weeks, not the longer-acting Eylea HD and Vabysmo; patients must manage steroid eye drops; and it launches a year after sura-vec into aflibercept biosimilars
column12: the 1/6 multiple is the most arguable figure here.
